options: Installs the Az module for the first time
Opens a browser window for interactive sign-in to Azure, then reports the connected account, subscription, and tenant
Permanently deletes your current Azure session history
Only works if you are already inside Azure Cloud Shell
questions.explain: It's the one-line command that authenticates a local PowerShell session against Azure.

questions.q: Why is it worth checking the output of Connect-AzAccount before running further commands?
options: The output is purely cosmetic and has no practical use
It automatically switches you to the Dev-Sandbox subscription
If you have access to more than one subscription, it tells you which one you landed in — worth confirming before creating or deleting anything
It shows your Windows password in plain text
questions.explain: Landing in the wrong subscription before running a create/delete command is a real, avoidable mistake.

questions.q: What makes Azure Cloud Shell a genuinely useful zero-install option?
options: It requires installing the full Az module locally before it can be used
It only supports Bash, never PowerShell
It's a browser-based shell built into the Azure Portal that's already signed in as you, with Az already loaded — no local install required
It is slower and less capable than a local install in every way
questions.explain: Cloud Shell is pre-authenticated and pre-loaded, useful for quick checks or machines you don't want to configure.

questions.q: What does Cloud Shell's first-run setup prompt actually configure?
options: A firewall rule allowing external connections to your VM
A small storage account to persist files (scripts, output) between Cloud Shell sessions
A new Azure subscription with billing enabled
A permanent password reset for your Azure account
questions.explain: The storage account is what lets your files survive between Cloud Shell sessions — a one-time step per subscription.

questions.q: Why does running Disconnect-AzAccount matter on a shared machine?
options: It has no real security implication and is purely optional cleanup
It deletes the Az module from the machine entirely
It is required before Connect-AzAccount can ever be run again
An open Az session left signed in is a real, avoidable exposure, especially if that account has production access
questions.explain: Leaving an authenticated session open on a shared machine is comparable to not logging out of any other sensitive account.
